purpose: Authoritative Microsoft documentation delta promoting Dynamics 365 Business Central to spec verification and defining cloud/on-prem source-scope, paging, webhook and read-authority constraints. Reuses REST/OpenAPI/OData/webhook fabric. No credentials, customer data, production mutation, private-network access or paid services were used.

patch.evidenceNote: Microsoft documents Business Central API v2.0 over REST/OData, cloud environment and company scoping, OAuth/S2S access, server-driven paging, throttling/recovery guidance and webhook subscriptions. Online APIs are enabled by default; on-premises endpoints are customer-managed and APIs must be enabled by an administrator. No sandbox or tenant authentication was performed, so this promotion is specification evidence only.
securityEvidenceBlockers: Service-to-service access requires an Entra application permission named API.ReadWrite.All even for a read-only WFM integration. Before authentication evidence advances, prove a dedicated Business Central application identity with narrowly assigned Business Central permission sets and effective denied mutations; the Entra scope name itself is not proof of read authority.

Business Central resource APIs can expose POST, PATCH, DELETE and business actions as well as GET. Steady-state WFM must use executor-enforced exact read-route and method allowlists; successful bearer authentication is not evidence of least privilege.

On-premises Business Central endpoints are customer-managed and may sit behind private networks/firewalls. WFM must use an authorised customer-edge/TLS route and never directly scan or bridge the private network; legacy Basic/access-key authentication must not be preferred when an approved OAuth/S2S deployment is available.

The Business Central application contains manufacturing data such as production orders, BOMs, routings, work centres and machine centres, but standard API v2 documentation does not establish complete standard endpoints for those objects. WFM must not infer API availability from application functionality; manufacturing enrichment requires a separately verified custom API, published OData/query, analytics/export or middleware route.

Webhook subscription creation and three-day renewal are mutating control-plane operations. Normal read-only runtime cannot silently acquire that authority; use customer-controlled provisioning/renewal or continue polling and reconciliation.

requiredPermissions: dedicated Microsoft Entra application or delegated identity authorised for the intended Business Central tenant/environment only
narrow Business Central application permission sets for required read objects; do not assign SUPER and prove mutations are denied
pin api.businesscentral.dynamics.com for cloud or an explicitly approved customer-edge endpoint for on-premises; prohibit arbitrary hosts and redirects
scope every read and checkpoint by connection plus tenant/environment/company for cloud, or serverInstance/company for on-premises
if webhooks are used, separate customer-approved subscription creation/renewal authority from steady-state read credentials and bind clientState to the expected source scope
dataAvailableOrExpected: companies/environments including tenant/environment identity and environment country code for source routing/provenance
employee reference records from the standard API where authorised; these enrich identity/organisation but do not replace authoritative HCM contracts, skills, absence or payroll
items/SKUs and item ledger entries including posting date, quantity, source/document references, actual sales amount, actual cost amount and last-modified timestamp
general ledger entries including account, posting date, document references, debit/credit and last-modified timestamp for finance attribution
purchase orders and lines plus related vendor/procurement context available through standard API resources
standard company-scoped master/transaction resources supported by API v2.0, subject to the assigned Business Central permission sets

production orders, BOMs, routings, work centres, machine centres, material consumption/output and production cost context only when an authorised customer custom API/OData/query/export surface explicitly exposes them; do not assume standard v2 coverage
stableIdentifiers: preserve provider SystemId/GUID identifiers from API v2.0 as source keys where supplied
namespace every source ID by connection plus tenant/environment/company or on-prem serverInstance/company because the same business number can exist in multiple companies/environments
preserve document numbers, item numbers, employee numbers and account numbers as business matching aids, never as cross-company global IDs

freshnessLatency.restOData: WFM-controlled polling bounded by Business Central throttling and server-driven paging; use last-modified filters only where the specific resource contract exposes them
freshnessLatency.webhooks: default delivery is delayed about 30 seconds and may collapse high-volume changes into a collection notification; subscriptions expire after three days and provider retries qualifying failures for up to 36 hours, so read reconciliation remains mandatory
freshnessLatency.onPrem: latency and limits are deployment-configured and must be measured in the customer environment rather than inherited from cloud assumptions

paginationDeltaEvents.pagination: use provider server-driven paging/next links; do not implement deep client paging with $top/$skip
paginationDeltaEvents.delta: use reviewed lastModifiedDateTime or equivalent filters only on resources that publish them, with overlap windows, stable-ID dedupe and checkpoint scope binding
paginationDeltaEvents.webhooks: validationToken handshake is mandatory; optional clientState can authenticate/bind notifications but events remain a low-latency signal rather than completeness authority
paginationDeltaEvents.reconciliation: checkpoint only after complete provider pages; a scope, company, environment, API version or dataset change creates a new checkpoint namespace and requires overlap replay/reconciliation

rateLimitsAndRetries: 429 and 503 require bounded cool-off/backoff with jitter for idempotent reads; do not broaden scope, switch company or alter auth in response to throttling
504 requires splitting long-running reads into smaller bounded requests rather than blind repetition
queue bursty shift-change/backfill traffic so small tenants stay lightweight while large multi-company tenants do not amplify provider throttling
401/403 enter credential/permission diagnostics and stop blind retry; they never trigger API downgrade or permission expansion
versionsRegionsCustomFields: pin standard API v2.0 or an explicitly versioned custom API route and preserve version in lineage/checkpoints

cloud environment discovery returns tenant identity, environment type/name and countryCode; preserve these values as provenance but do not infer contractual data-residency guarantees from countryCode alone
on-premises API availability/auth/limits are deployment-specific and APIs are disabled by default until an administrator enables them
standard Business Central APIs cannot be extended with additional fields; custom/customer fields require a separately versioned custom API or other authorised published surface
preserve source currency, units, locale, timezone and date semantics; conversion or FX normalisation stays in the canonical semantic layer with dated provenance
automationOpportunities: bootstrap company, item, supplier, procurement and finance dimensions from one common SMB/mid-market ERP connection to reduce implementation mapping effort
join item/material and purchase-order context to workforce availability/skills to distinguish material-constrained work from labour-constrained work before overtime or agency labour is committed

join authoritative WFM pay/attendance cost to Business Central item/production/finance evidence for labour-per-order, labour-per-good-unit and cost-centre attribution without treating ERP employee or ledger records as payroll truth
use company/environment discovery to configure multi-entity integrations without assuming one Business Central environment equals one legal entity
use read reconciliation after throttling, webhook collection notifications or regional/environment outages so executive reporting exposes data freshness rather than silently presenting partial data
savingsHypotheses: reduce implementation effort for Business Central manufacturers by auto-discovering environments/companies and reusing the same REST/OData fabric instead of building company-specific point integrations
reduce paid idle time and avoidable overtime by separating material/procurement blockers from genuine workforce-capacity constraints before shifts are finalised
improve payroll/finance reconciliation and labour-cost attribution by preserving Business Central company/account/item/document IDs alongside authoritative WFM attendance and pay evidence

reduce multi-entity reporting errors by preventing checkpoints and source identifiers from leaking across tenants, environments or companies after acquisitions, sandbox-to-production moves or regional restructuring
causalOutcomeReadiness: preserve connection, tenant, environment/serverInstance, company, source SystemId, API version, dataset, source/effective timestamp, ingestion timestamp and schema fingerprint on every mapped record
preserve recommendation/action identifiers and baseline/outcome windows when labour is redeployed in response to inventory, procurement or production signals

retain competing changes such as purchase receipts, inventory movements, order releases, production status, cost postings and company/environment changes so an outcome is not falsely attributed to a staffing recommendation
dataGaps: no authorised Business Central sandbox/tenant was available to prove Entra application binding, effective Business Central permission sets, denied writes, real company visibility, paging, throttling or read round trips
standard API v2.0 does not establish complete manufacturing/MRP object coverage; production objects require a customer custom API/OData/query/export or middleware surface and separate evidence
standard APIs cannot simply be extended with customer fields, so custom field coverage is tenant-extension specific
webhooks require mutating subscription create/renew operations and can emit collection notifications, so polling/reconciliation remains required for completeness
on-premises hosts, auth, API enablement, network topology and limits vary by deployment and require customer-edge proof
constraintsRisks: S2S tokens use an Entra application scope named API.ReadWrite.All, making effective Business Central object permissions and exact runtime method allowlists critical for a genuinely read-only integration
company/environment ambiguity can create silent cross-entity corruption if source IDs or checkpoints are reused without scope partitioning
on-premises Business Central may use legacy auth and private network exposure patterns that WFM must not normalize into direct cloud connectivity
429/503/504 and webhook collection notifications require queueing, backoff and reconciliation at enterprise scale
manufacturing functionality visible in the Business Central application must never be presented as API-integrated until its custom/published interface has separate evidence
valueReview.nextDevelopmentAction: Use an authorised Business Central sandbox to prove a dedicated Microsoft Entra application plus narrow Business Central permission sets, environment/company discovery, exact GET-only route authority, v2.0 server-driven paging, 401/403/429/503/504 recovery, source-scope checkpoint isolation, and real item-ledger/general-ledger/purchase-order reads. Prove mutations are denied. Only test webhook subscription bootstrap or manufacturing custom APIs when separately authorised; keep on-premises access behind a customer edge and keep all business/payroll mutations disabled.
